# CLAIMs with `line` `readiness`

*Lines of inquiry — A named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found. Retracting a line is a status change on its members, never a deletion (ADR-032).*

**Readiness and slack** — what it takes to keep, reach and pay for capacities whose value lies in rare circumstances — readiness as response capability, slack and reconfiguration slack as different reserves, the resource threshold of a transition and its obstructions, and budget rules that remove options no one chose to give up (ADR-073). When transient support can be withdrawn is a line of its own (ADR-087).

The threshold of [CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md) is the least, over admissible paths, of each path's peak requirement, and both the peak and the least move by at most the largest error in the requirement. So a planner who knows each configuration's cost to within ε knows a transition's threshold to within ε, and its reconfiguration slack to within 2ε. The error is also one-sided in a useful way: overestimating only raises the threshold, and underestimating anywhere can only lower it, possibly by opening a cheaper path that does not exist. | [CLAIM-878](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-878.md) v2 | Under a budget set each period to the last period's peak spending, a capability stays funded exactly as long as every period contains a mobilization at its cost, whether a use, a drill, a false alarm or a cancelled dispatch, so dispatching it provisionally to every report keeps it funded far longer than dispatching it only on confirmation of need | A corollary of [CLAIM-577](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-577.md), found in running [LEAD-080](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-080.md)'s study ([CASE-315](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-315.md)). Under spend-matching the next budget is this period's peak, so a capability costing B* to mobilize stays affordable exactly as long as every period has something that mobilizes it, and its first period with nothing loses it for good. If q_t is the chance that period t has nothing, the chance of losing it within n periods is 1 − ∏(1 − q_t). Whatever mobilizes counts: a use, a drill, a false alarm or a provisional dispatch ([TERM-109](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-109.md)) cancelled minutes later. So the dispatch policy decides how long the capability survives the rule. Sent provisionally to six reports a month, a heavy rescue squad is quiet in a month with chance e^(−6) and was still funded after nine years in 80 % of the study's runs; sent only on confirmation it was lost in every run within months. | [CLAIM-921](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-921.md) v2 | Where competence decays without funded maintenance and a capability is committed only when competent enough, a budget that follows observed use has a state in which the capability is never used or funded again whenever the base budget alone sustains competence below that level, any stretch without occasions long enough for competence to decay there reaches it whatever each use was paid, so at the same expected funding a rarer capability is lost sooner, while maintenance funded apart from use, at a level that sustains the threshold, has no such state | Found in running [LEAD-036](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-036.md)'s study ([CASE-343](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-343.md)) of A's model from [QUESTION-386](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-386.md). A stretch without occasions long enough for k to decay from its ceiling below k_lo reaches that state whatever earlier uses earned, so the chance of loss has a lower bound that rises as occasions grow rarer and does not depend on η: paying more per use does not make up for rarity.
